_README: Canonical bench registry for this machine. ONE copy, at
C:/dev/qmx-panadapter/tools/bench.json - every worktree reads it by
absolute path. Never copy it into another tree; edit it here.
Paths use forward slashes deliberately: PowerShell accepts them and it
keeps this file free of backslash escaping.
Runtime state (who holds the build lock, who holds the antenna) lives in
the lock file, NOT here. This file is the plan; the lock is the moment.

antenna.note: One antenna, two radios, a 2-way switch. Only ONE bench is on air at a time. The spare switch position feeds a dummy load, so a TX on the off-antenna bench is safe. Record the holder with 'bench antenna <name>' - decode counts and noise floor from the antenna-less bench are meaningless.

benches.name: bench1
benches.name_note: WAS CALLED 'dev' until 2026-10-28, and most of the notes, commit messages and memory files in this project still say 'the dev bench' - they mean THIS board, Tab5 #1, MAC 30:ED:A0:EA:DD:57 on COM5. Renamed on the operator's instruction once bench2 arrived and the dev/bench naming collided. Its capture moved with it: scratchpad/capture-dev.txt is now capture-bench1.txt, same file, 783 MB of history carried over by rename, not copy.
benches.role: MAIN, on v1.20.5-31-g0cf92aeb (flashed 2026-10-24). Runs the newest main commit and is the bench every release is flasher-verified on. Standing PASSIVE capture (no -Reset) to scratchpad/capture-dev.txt - leave it running; it is the only record of a crash that happens while nobody is watching.
role_note: tree/branch below describe WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON IT, because that is
what 'bench flash dev' builds from. A stale entry here does not read
as wrong - it silently flashes the other tree's firmware over this
one and then PASSES the MAC verify, because the board is the right
board. That is the one thing in this entry worth re-reading.
This bench has been loaned out before (Track A, the Tab5-native RX
audio work in C:/dev/qmx-panadapter-audio on feat/rx-audio-output)
and reclaimed the same day. If it is loaned again, change tree and
branch here at the same time, not afterwards.
It still carries util/sock_owners.c, the LWIP socket-owner dump from
#313 - it fires on a new high-water mark and on exhaustion. #313
itself is CLOSED (it was the arithmetic: max_open_sockets 13 -> 8),
so the dump is now background instrumentation rather than an active
soak. Nothing is waiting on it.
benches.ip_note: STATIC since 2026-10-24 - the operator pinned it, so this is no longer a lease that drifts and no longer needs re-checking every session. It moved .210 -> .211 -> .209 -> .210 in the weeks before that and every stale entry cost a timeout read as a dead board. The board still prints its own address at boot (sta ip: in its capture) and that stays the authority if this is ever wrong. qmx.local is NOT a discriminator: every unit answers to it, and on 2026-08-27 it resolved to a different board entirely.
benches.com_note: Was COM3 on the old laptop; re-verified by MAC (30:ED:A0:EA:DD:57) on the Ryzen box 2026-09-03, enumerated as COM5 there instead. COM follows the socket, not the board - re-check on any machine change.
benches.radio_note: Swapped 2026-09-05: was the small QMX. That radio's finals were worn down by WSPR TX at FULL power (110 s of key-down every 120 s) until it drew excessive current on plain RX; it is away being re-finalled. This is the real-world case the WSPR PA guard exists for - CLAUDE.md measures the finals at 4.69 W unguarded vs 1.12 W at the 6.0 V target. The QMX+ here reports 'QMX GPS source: QMX+ Internal' at CAT link-up and its second-tick phase-locks to SNTP within ~10 ms, so time_src reads GPS legitimately on this bench (NOT the #173 false-GPS case).

benches.name: field
benches.ip_note: DHCP. Was .178 and had drifted by 2026-10-10 - found by sweeping the subnet for /api/status. The board prints its own address at boot; this field is a convenience, not the authority.
benches.com_note: ⛔ TEMPORARY. COM10 is the WAVESHARE's socket - he unplugged that board and put this Tab5 on its USB-C on 2026-10-10 for the two-station JS8 test. COM FOLLOWS THE SOCKET, NOT THE BOARD, so this number stops being true the moment either board is moved back. MAC-verified 80:F1:B2:D1:45:92 while it was there. VERIFY BY MAC BEFORE FLASHING ANYTHING HERE. This field previously said UNASSIGNED while the board was plugged in and talking, which cost a subnet sweep; writing a borrowed socket in as if it were permanent would be the same mistake in the other direction.
benches.radio_note: Added 2026-10-10 as the second station for the JS8 two-station test. NOTE its QMX firmware is 1_04_004, older than dev's 1_04_010.
benches.tree: n/a - runs the last RELEASE, EXCEPT when borrowed as station 2. Point it at the main checkout ONLY for a deliberate cable flash, then put it back.
benches.usb_flash_reason: PREFER OTA on this unit: it is the board that proves the update path a real user takes, so an OTA result here is worth more than on dev. Cable-flash it only when a test needs it, and expect to re-establish the OTA evidence afterwards.
benches.usb_flash_history: CABLE-FLASHED 2026-10-10 a FIFTH time, to v1.16.12-108-g35dde707 (seven-stack hardening + the JS8 free-text decode-count fixes), at his explicit request after he tore the field station down and before setting it up again. It was on v1.16.12-102-g73e849ba. MAC-verified 80:f1:b2:d1:45:92 BEFORE writing with 'bench verify field' (COM10 is the WAVESHARE socket - this is not optional) and again after. ⛔ IT TOOK TWO DELIBERATE bench.json EDITS, both reverted: usb_flash NO->yes, and tree pointed at the main checkout because tree is PROSE on this bench, so bench.ps1 Push-Location throws on it. ⚠ REVERTING THE TREE BIT ME: a plain string replace of "C:/dev/qmx-panadapter" hits DEV first, because dev legitimately has that exact path - so dev and field ended up with each other's tree and the file still looked plausible. That is the silent-wrong-tree trap dev's own role_note warns about. Recovered with git checkout, not by hand. IF YOU FIND usb_flash=yes OR A REAL PATH IN tree ON THIS BENCH, a session died mid-flash - put them back, and verify ALL THREE benches afterwards. ⚠ OTA EVIDENCE STALE - re-establish at the next release. CABLE-FLASHED 2026-10-10 a FOURTH time, to v1.16.12-102-g73e849ba (JS8 free-text TX + the transmission-type fix). MAC-verified 80:f1:b2:d1:45:92 on COM10 first, as com_note demands. ⚠ OTA EVIDENCE STALE - re-establish at the next release. CABLE-FLASHED 2026-10-10 a THIRD time, to v1.16.12-98-g0fa5f7e2 (waterfall window 2/200 + SNR recalibrated to jt9). MAC-verified 80:f1:b2:d1:45:92 on COM10 before writing, as com_note demands. ⚠ THE OTA EVIDENCE ON THIS UNIT IS STALE - re-establish it at the next release. CABLE-FLASHED 2026-10-10 AGAIN to put v1.16.12-96-gf25a9e95 on it (decode-dedup + the 4-char grid fix); MAC-verified 80:f1:b2:d1:45:92 on COM10 before writing, as com_note demands. ⚠ THE OTA EVIDENCE ON THIS UNIT IS NOW STALE - re-establish it at the next release. Earlier: CABLE-FLASHED 2026-10-10 to put v1.16.12-79-g9fc8113e on it for the two-station JS8 test (memory project_js8_j6_tx_decoded_by_second_station). This field used to claim the unit had NEVER been USB-flashed; that was never literally true - every board is cable-flashed to receive its first firmware, as he pointed out when I quoted this line back at him as a reason not to proceed. Prose in a registry is not evidence.

benches.name: bench2
benches.role: CW BRANCH. Tab5 #3, unboxed 2026-10-28 and taken straight onto feat/cw-page so dev (COM5) goes back to the main track. The operator named it.
benches.mac_note: Read with `esptool -p COM16 read_mac` BEFORE the first write, while the board was factory-fresh and had no boot header to check. Two away from field 80:f1:b2:d1:45:92 - same batch. dev is 30:ED:A0:EA:DD:57 and is NOT this board.
benches.ip_note: DHCP, first seen 2026-10-28 right after the first flash. ⚠ I predicted this unit could NOT reach the network, because the flash was a full erase and NVS should have carried no credentials. It associated with BV50 at -28 dBm anyway, so that prediction was wrong and the credentials came from somewhere I have not identified. It prints its own address as sta ip: in its capture once it associates, and THAT is the authority, not this field.
benches.com_note: Enumerated as COM16 on first plug 2026-10-28. COM FOLLOWS THE SOCKET, NOT THE BOARD - re-verify by MAC if anything is moved.
benches.usb_flash_history: FIRST FLASH 2026-10-28: erase_flash then write_flash of v1.22.0-90-ge6cdf310 (feat/cw-page, carrying the esp_hosted sync-RPC table lock). MAC-verified 80:f1:b2:d1:42:ca before the erase, since a factory board has no boot header to check afterwards.
